title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI hook for prompt-set regression checks and metric gating
author: Asha Patel
description: Add a per-prompt CI hook that runs prompt-set regressions and gates merges by eval metrics. Motivation: teams keep introducing subtle prompt changes that degrade quality for specific prompts; a per-prompt CI hook lets us fail fast on regressions and attach metric diffs to PRs. This PR implements a lightweight CI hook and optional metric gating policy that can be configured per-repo or org-wide. Changes include a new hook binary, a reusable GitHub Actions workflow, a small config schema for prompt groups and thresholds, and end-to-end tests. Checklist: - [x] implement per_prompt_ci runner and CLI - [x] add GitHub Actions workflow and matrix for supported runtimes - [x] add config schema and example repos/prompt-sets - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs and usage examples - [x] telemetry/metrics for gating decisions How it works: when the hook runs it collects the candidate prompt-set, executes eval-harness against a pinned baseline model set, computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy/utility/consistency) and compares to historical baselines; if any prompt metric breaches configured thresholds the hook marks the job as failed and uploads a compact JSON report and HTML summary artifact. The gating is optional and controlled by ci/prompt_ci.yml and the eval-harness config. Backwards compatibility: hook is opt-in and default configs are non-blocking. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the threshold semantics and the artifact retention policy. Related Linear: ENG-4821 ENG-4890.
